The Sun, for instance, bends starlight by less than two arcseconds, a tiny amount barely detectable without precise instruments. When you look at Earth or other planets through a telescope, the image distortion you might see usually comes from atmospheric turbulence (making stars twinkle) or optical imperfections in the lens, not from gravity warping space-time around the planet itself.
